title and abstract.summary: The study measured the relationship between various functional traits (body size, phenology, nesting location, sociality, and foraging choice) and the prevalence of three pathogens (trypanosomes, neogregarines, and Nosema ceranae) across wild bee communities, and also examined intra-specific size variation in Bombus impatiens. The study investigates how functional traits, such as body size and phenology, might influence pathogen prevalence in bee communities, using Bombus impatiens as an example.
